facts.fact: Adwave says Facebook and Instagram ad budgets for local events can start around $5 per day.
facts.quote: Budget flexibility starting around $5/day

facts.fact: Adwave says a streaming TV campaign for local events starts at $30 a day.
facts.quote: streaming TV campaign starting at $30 a day

facts.fact: The page says local event marketers can run streaming TV commercials on Hulu, Peacock, and Tubi targeted only to viewers in their area.
facts.quote: You can now run commercials on services like Hulu, Peacock, and Tubi targeting only viewers in your area.

facts.fact: The page recommends Facebook and Instagram ads for events with strong visual appeal that target audiences aged 25 and up.
facts.quote: Events with strong visual appeal targeting audiences 25+.

facts.fact: The page describes streaming TV advertising as an awareness channel rather than a direct-response channel.
facts.quote: Awareness channel, not direct response

facts.fact: The page cites industry benchmarks suggesting local event marketing should be 20-30% of projected ticket revenue.
facts.quote: Industry benchmarks suggest 20-30% of projected ticket revenue for marketing, but this varies widely.

facts.fact: For events with established audiences, the page recommends allocating 40% of the marketing budget to retention (email and past attendee outreach).
facts.quote: 40% on retention (email, past attendee outreach)

facts.fact: For events with established audiences, the page recommends allocating 30% of the marketing budget to paid advertising to expand reach.
facts.quote: 30% on paid advertising to expand reach

facts.fact: For events with established audiences, the page recommends allocating 20% of the marketing budget to partnerships and cross-promotions.

facts.fact: For events with established audiences, the page recommends allocating 10% of the marketing budget to PR and earned media.
facts.quote: 10% on PR and earned media

facts.fact: For new events building awareness from scratch, the page recommends allocating 50% of the marketing budget to paid advertising (streaming TV, social, search).

facts.fact: For new events building awareness from scratch, the page recommends allocating 25% of the marketing budget to partnerships with established local organizations.

facts.fact: The page advises beginning event marketing 8-12 weeks before significant events.
facts.quote: Begin 8-12 weeks out for significant events.

facts.fact: The page says smaller community events might need only 4-6 weeks of promotion before the date.
facts.quote: Smaller community events might need only 4-6 weeks.

facts.quote: Reserve any paid budget for the final 2-3 weeks to drive urgency

facts.fact: The page states that starting heavy promotion two weeks before an event rarely works.
